---
title: "ADR 0001: Maintain technical documentation with Quarto"
status: accepted
date: 2026-07-31
---

## Context

NADABAS has short Markdown developer guides and a larger technical draft in
Microsoft Word. The project needs documentation that is easy to review with
source changes, searchable for readers, and still available as a consolidated
document for organisational use.

## Decision

Maintain the technical documentation as a Quarto book below `docs/`.

- Markdown and Quarto source files are reviewed in normal pull requests.
- HTML is the primary reading format.
- DOCX is a generated output, not the source of truth.
- GitHub Pages is the intended static hosting platform after the build has been
  validated in CI.
- GitHub-recognised community files such as `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`,
  issue forms, and pull request templates remain in their conventional
  repository locations.
- The existing Word draft is migrated incrementally. Each section must be
  verified against the version-controlled VBA source and supported database
  design before publication.

## Consequences

- Contributors need Quarto to preview or render the complete documentation.
- Pull requests can review documentation and implementation together.
- The project can publish searchable HTML and produce a consolidated Word
  document from the same chapter structure.
- Rendered output directories must not be committed.
- Documentation rendering and link validation should become required CI checks
  after the initial structure has been reviewed.

## Alternatives considered

### Markdown files viewed only in GitHub

This has the lowest setup cost but becomes difficult to navigate and search as
the technical documentation grows.

### MkDocs

MkDocs is a strong option for an HTML-only developer site. It was not selected
because consolidated Word output remains useful for NADABAS.

### GitHub Wiki

A wiki separates documentation history and review from the ordinary source
workflow. It is not used as the authoritative technical source.
